known.title: Decision 2 raises the comment page to first:250 as the GraphQL connection maximum, but the GitHub GraphQL API accepts first only from 1 to 100, so every query that reads comments fails
known.summary: Decision 2 sets the comment page size to `first:250` and calls 250 the GraphQL connection maximum. The GitHub GraphQL docs (https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/overview/rate-limits-and-query-limits-for-the-graphql-api#node-limit) say: "Values of `first` and `last` must be within 1-100." A live query of issue 69 with `comments(first:250)` returns the EXCESSIVE_PAGINATION error "Requesting 250 records on the `comments` connection exceeds the `first` limit of 100 records.", and gh exits non-zero. At repo_ref, plan.mjs builds the comments connection with issueConnectionSelection (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs, lines 76-77), `show` and `archive` read comments (lines 688 and 853), and graphql() fails on any `errors` entry (line 59). So with this decision, `show` and `archive` fail on every plan, A3 cannot pass, and the 100 MB size estimate and the 256 MiB buffer rest on a page size that GitHub rejects. The page size must stay at 100.

known.title: Step 1 must change the fake gh stub to write output synchronously, but its Files cell does not list scripts/tests/fixtures/gh-stub/gh, and no other row does
known.locator: Steps, row 1 helper_fixes, Files cell (line 64); Research, #68 stub fact (line 19)
known.summary: Row 1 Task adds "a stub that writes all output", and Research (line 19) says that a regression test above 1 MiB needs synchronous writes in `scripts/tests/fixtures/gh-stub/gh`, because the stub prints with console.log and then calls process.exit(0), which delivered only 146,176 of 8,388,608 bytes. At repo_ref the stub does that (scripts/tests/fixtures/gh-stub/gh, lines 161-163, 241-243, 425-427, and more). But the row 1 Files cell lists only plan.mjs and scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs, and no other row names the stub. plan-contract.md at repo_ref (Steps, acceptance, and effects, line 62) says "`Files` defines scope." So the stub edit is out of the plan's scope: an implementer who keeps to Files cannot make the large-output case of the row 1 Done when pass, and a stub edit is an unplanned change for code review.

known.title: Acceptance A5 uses a plain `- [HIGH]` finding line that the unfixed v0.11.1 parser already reads as fixes-required, so A5 passes when the bolded-severity fix of #49 is missing
known.locator: Acceptance, row A5 (line 77); Goal, #49 (line 7); Research, #49 rows (line 24)
known.summary: The Goal (line 7) says that a bolded severe finding cannot keep a code pass, and Research (line 24) shows that `- **[HIGH]** ...` after `Code-review: pass` fails open. A5 now tests `- [HIGH] Bug - src/example.mjs:1 - data loss - fix` without emphasis. At repo_ref, parseReviewComment already matches that line with the severity regex `^\s*(?:[-*]\s+)?(?:\[(?:critical|high)\]|(?:critical|high):)` (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs, line 615). A run of the repo_ref parser prints {"kind":"code","verdict":"fixes-required"} for the A5 text, and {"kind":"code","verdict":"pass"} for the bolded form. A4 checks only a bolded verdict line. So no Acceptance row fails when step 1 leaves the bolded, numbered, or quoted severity fail-open in place, against plan-contract.md (line 65: Acceptance rows cover the goal).

known.title: Decision 1 says that `gh issue reopen --comment` applies the comment and the reopen together or not at all and is safe to rerun, but gh posts the comment and then runs a separate reopen mutation
known.summary: The reopen flow after a partial merge relies on one `gh issue reopen --comment` call being all-or-nothing and safe to rerun. The gh manual (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue_reopen) only says "Add a reopening comment" and gives no atomic behavior. The gh source (https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/v2.102.0/pkg/cmd/issue/reopen/reopen.go, lines 92-111) first posts the comment with CommentableRun (line 102) and then sends a separate reopenIssue mutation with apiReopen (line 108); when the issue is already open it returns early and posts no comment (lines 87-90). So a failure between the two writes leaves the issue closed (finished) with a comment that says it was reopened, and the rerun that the decision allows posts a second reopening comment. The contract text that step 2 writes from this decision then gives the manager a wrong recovery for a partial failure.
